questions.prompt: Which HTTP status code is most appropriate when a client successfully creates a new resource via a POST request?

options.text: 200 OK
201 Created
204 No Content
303 See Other

questions.explanation: Status code 201 Created explicitly indicates that the request has succeeded and led to the creation of a resource, often accompanied by a Location header pointing to the new entry.

questions.prompt: Why is API versioning important for public-facing web services?

options.text: It guarantees that response payloads will always be smaller in size.
It prevents breaking changes from immediately failing existing client integrations.
It eliminates the need to document query parameters.
It automatically converts XML responses into JSON format.

questions.explanation: API versioning allows developers to introduce breaking changes without disrupting active clients, giving them time to migrate to the new version at their own pace.

questions.prompt: When designing a RESTful API for a blogging platform, which endpoint best represents retrieving comments for a specific post?

options.text: GET /posts?id=5&include=comments
GET /getCommentsByPostId?postId=5
GET /posts/5/comments
GET /comments/post/5

questions.explanation: Nested resources in REST are best expressed hierarchically using path parameters, clearly showing the relationship where comments belong to a specific post.

questions.prompt: What is the primary benefit of designing APIs with HATEOAS (Hypermedia As The Engine Of Application State)?

options.text: It encrypts the payload for improved transport security.
It reduces the total number of network round-trips required.
It allows clients to dynamically discover available actions through returned links rather than hardcoding URLs.
It enforces strict typing on all query parameters.

questions.explanation: HATEOAS provides links in the response body, enabling clients to navigate the API dynamically without needing prior knowledge of the endpoint structure.

questions.prompt: How should a well-designed API handle partial updates to a resource where only a subset of fields are modified?

options.text: Use the PUT method with only the updated fields in the body.
Use the PATCH method with a JSON Merge Patch or JSON Patch payload.
Use the POST method with a special 'update' query parameter.
Use the GET method to pass updated fields via query strings.

questions.explanation: The PATCH method is semantically designed for partial updates, whereas PUT is traditionally meant for complete resource replacement.

questions.prompt: Which strategy is most robust for handling high-volume write requests and preventing duplicate resource creation due to network retries?

options.text: Requiring clients to pass a unique idempotency key header for state-changing requests.
Relying exclusively on auto-incrementing integer IDs generated by the database.
Converting all POST requests into GET requests to leverage browser caching.
Increasing the timeout threshold on the server load balancer.

questions.explanation: Idempotency keys allow clients to safely retry failed requests without accidentally creating duplicate records, as the server tracks and deduplicates requests using the key.
